4.  **Processing 3D Volumes (Single Frame):** If $d.shape.size() == 3$: resize `VolumeFrames` to 1; set `Shape` to $d.shape$; resize `Data` to $Shape[0] \times Shape[1] \times Shape[2]$; transform $d.data$ to `float`; find $MinValue = \min(d.data)$ and $MaxValue = \max(d.data)$; normalize by subtracting $MinValue$ from each element; set `IsTimeVaryingVolume` to `false` [S1, unofficial].

The claim describes the specific logic for processing a 3D volume (single frame) within a C++ class for loading .npy files. Source [S1] explicitly lists this logic in its notes: 'Handle 3D volume (single frame). Resize VolumeFrames to 1. Set Shape from d.shape. Resize Data to Shape[0]*Shape[1]*Shape[2]. Transform data to float. Find min/max elements. Set MinValue and MaxValue. Normalize data by subtracting MinValue from each element. Set IsTimeVaryingVolume to false.' All steps mentioned in the claim are present in the evidence provided in Source [S1].
supported

5.  **Processing 4D Volumes (Time-Varying):** If $d.shape.size() == 4$: set $N = d.shape[0]$, $X = d.shape[1]$, $Y = d.shape[2]$, $Z = d.shape[3]$; resize `VolumeFrames` to $N$; set `IsTimeVaryingVolume` to `true`; for each frame $t$ from $0$ to $N-1$: set `Shape` to $(X, Y, Z)$; resize `Data` to $X \times Y \times Z$; copy frame data from $d.data$; transform to `float`; find $MinValue_t = \min(\text{frame}_t)$ and $MaxValue_t = \max(\text{frame}_t)$; set `MinValue` and `MaxValue`; normalize by subtracting $MinValue_t$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim describes the specific logic for processing 4D volumes (time-varying) as detailed in the 'Source [S1] notes' section. The notes explicitly state: 'Handle 4D volume (time-varying)... For each frame t, set Shape, resize Data, copy frame data from d.data, transform to float, find min/max, set MinValue/MaxValue, normalize by subtracting MinValue. Set IsTimeVaryingVolume to true.' This matches the steps outlined in the claim exactly. Although the 'Source [S1] passages' provided are snippets of JSON configuration code unrelated to the volume loading logic, the 'notes' section is part of the provided source material and fully supports the claim.
